skill.name: using-git-worktrees
skill.description: Creates isolated Git worktrees with directory selection, ignore checks, setup detection, and baseline verification.
skill.summary: Set up safe, isolated Git worktrees for feature work without disturbing the current checkout.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, inline command examples, stderr redirects, and documented worktree paths. The main residual risk is that the skill can run project setup and test commands automatically, which is unsafe in untrusted repositories without confirmation.

remediation.issue: Automatic setup and test command execution
remediation.suggestion: Ask for user confirmation before dependency installation, build, download, or test commands in untrusted repositories.
Show the planned .gitignore change and ask before committing it to the repository.
Ask before writing outside the repository and resolve the global path explicitly before creation.

static_findings.snippet: **If found:** Use that directory. If both exist, `.worktrees` wins.
- **Fix:** Always use `git check-ignore` before creating project-local worktree

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Project Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent to auto-detect and run dependency installation, build, download, and test commands after creating a worktree. In untrusted repositories, those commands can execute project-controlled scripts without a clear confirmation step.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are explicitly listed in the setup and baseline sections, and the text says to auto-detect and run them. The risk depends on repository trust, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Repository Mutation Without Explicit Approval
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs the agent to add a worktree ignore rule and commit the change when a project-local directory is not ignored. This can alter repository history before the user has approved that specific commit.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction to add and commit the change is direct. The purpose is protective, so this is a workflow safety issue rather than evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Developers need isolated branches without disturbing their current workspace. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe worktree setup and baseline checks.
actual_capabilities: Chooses an existing .worktrees or worktrees directory using a documented priority order.
Checks CLAUDE.md for a project-specific worktree directory preference.
Verifies project-local worktree directories are ignored before creation.
Creates a new Git worktree and switches into it.
Runs setup and test commands based on detected project files.
Reports the worktree path and baseline test status.
limitations: Requires a Git repository with worktree support available.
Dependency setup and tests may execute project-controlled commands.
Does not merge, clean up, or remove worktrees after feature work.
Directory choice may require user input when no project preference exists.

use_cases.title: Feature Branch Isolation
use_cases.description: Create a separate workspace for implementation while keeping the current checkout untouched.

use_cases.title: Parallel Review Work
use_cases.description: Open a bug fix or review branch beside active work without switching branches.

use_cases.title: Agent Workflow Preparation
use_cases.description: Prepare a clean worktree before an implementation plan runs through Claude, Codex, or Claude Code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Worktree
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an isolated Git worktree for this feature. Follow the project directory preference, verify ignore rules, and report the final path.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a worktree for feature/<name>. Check existing worktree directories and CLAUDE.md before asking me for a location.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare and Verify Baseline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a worktree for this task, run the detected setup steps, execute baseline tests, and stop if tests fail.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multiple Worktrees
prompt_templates.prompt: Create separate worktrees for implementation and release verification. Use project conventions, avoid tracked worktree directories, and summarize each workspace status.

output_examples.input: Create a worktree for an authentication feature.
output_examples.output: The response identifies the selected worktree directory, confirms ignore verification, reports the new branch, and summarizes baseline test status.

output_examples.input: No worktree directory exists in the repository.
output_examples.output: The response asks the user to choose between a project-local directory and the documented global location.
The response reports the failing test summary and asks whether to investigate or proceed with known failures.

best_practices: Verify ignore rules before creating project-local worktrees.
Ask before running setup commands in repositories you do not fully trust.
Record the final worktree path and baseline test result.
anti_patterns: Skipping CLAUDE.md or existing project conventions.
Continuing after failing baseline tests without user approval.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It creates an isolated Git workspace so feature work does not disturb the current checkout.

faq.question: Does it require Claude?
faq.answer: No. It is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when they can run Git commands.

faq.question: Does it create branches?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides creation of a new worktree with a new branch name.

faq.question: Can it use a global directory?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use ~/.config/superpowers/worktrees after user selection or project convention.

faq.question: Will it run project setup commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It suggests setup and test commands based on project files, so review them for untrusted repositories.

faq.question: Does it clean up worktrees?
faq.answer: No. Cleanup is outside this skill and should be handled by a finishing workflow.
